description: Fix answer parsing regex in both parseSolutions() (import script) and parseAnswers() (utility parser) to handle all CFA answer formats, and add comprehensive unit tests to verify all formats work correctly.
steps: Step 1: Fix parseSolutions() in src/scripts/import-questions.ts. The current regex ONLY matches 'N. X is correct'. Replace with a two-phase approach: (a) First split the solutions section into numbered blocks (same as parseProblems does), (b) Then within each block, try multiple patterns to extract the answer letter: 'X is correct', 'X.' at start, 'X ' at start (just a letter followed by space/explanation), or just a standalone letter 'X' followed by newline. The patterns to match IN ORDER OF SPECIFICITY: (1) /^([A-D])\s+is\s+correct/i, (2) /^([A-D])\.\s/  (letter + period + space), (3) /^([A-D])\s+(?!is)/  (letter + space, NOT followed by 'is' to avoid double-matching pattern 1), (4) /^([A-D])\s*$/m  (letter alone on a line). Extract explanation as the remaining text after the answer letter pattern.

Step 2: Fix parseAnswers() in src/features/question-bank/utils/question-parser.ts to use the same multi-pattern matching logic. Currently it already splits into numbered blocks, but the correctMatch logic within each block only tries: /^([A-D])\s+(?:is\s+)?correct/i, /correct\s+(?:answer[:\s]*)?([A-D])/i, and /^([A-D])\s*[.]/. Add the missing pattern: /^([A-D])\s/ (just a letter followed by whitespace with no 'correct' keyword). Also add /^([A-D])$/m for letter alone on line.

Step 3: Create test file src/features/question-bank/__tests__/question-parser.test.ts with comprehensive tests for parseAnswers() covering: (a) 'C is correct. Explanation' format (existing working format), (b) 'C. Explanation text' format (letter + period), (c) 'C Explanation text' format (just letter + space), (d) 'C\nExplanation text' format (letter on separate line), (e) Mixed formats in same text (some answers use one format, others use another), (f) Edge cases: lowercase letters, extra whitespace, multi-digit question numbers.

Step 4: Create test file src/scripts/__tests__/import-questions.test.ts testing the parseSolutions() function. Export parseSolutions from the import script (or refactor to make it testable). Test the same formats: 'X is correct', 'X.', 'X ' (letter+space), and 'X\n'. Verify that existing working subjects (like 'C is correct' format) still parse correctly.
Step 5: Run full verification: npx tsc --noEmit && npm run lint && npm run test && npm run build
acceptance_criteria: parseSolutions() in import-questions.ts matches answer format 'N. X is correct. Explanation...' (existing)
parseSolutions() matches 'N. X. Explanation...' (letter followed by period)
parseSolutions() matches 'N. X Explanation...' (letter followed by space then explanation)
parseSolutions() matches 'N. X\nExplanation...' (letter on its own followed by newline)
parseAnswers() in question-parser.ts matches all the same formats
All new tests pass via npm run test
TypeScript compiles cleanly via npx tsc --noEmit
Existing 'X is correct' format still works (no regression)
